title: AI influencer motion control workflow demo
author: tech_new_trends
key_info: A screen demo of an AI-influencer workflow: a node-graph (ComfyUI-style, shown on RunningHub AI) swaps a model's face into generated portraits and then runs a 'Motion Control' job that animated one image into a dance video in about 16 minutes. No steps, settings or models are explained, and the 'full workflow with guides' is behind a link or Telegram group. Nothing here could be checked beyond what is on screen. Note the content is photoreal AI personas built by face-swapping.

title: VoiceStudio open-source voice cloning
author: aiwithdivyam
key_info: VoiceStudio (debpalash/VoiceStudio) is a real open-source (AGPL-3.0) app for voice cloning, voice design, video dubbing, dictation, transcription and audiobooks, with 646 languages claimed. The repo showed about 80k stars (the reel says 79k). It runs locally on your machine (GPU or slower CPU); remote services are optional. Not confirmed: the '10 seconds of audio' for cloning and a flat 'no data ever leaves' claim. Link is only given by DM.

title: Rumble monetization with view-exchange app
author: startupgully
key_info: The reel shows a Rumble dashboard with $7.90 earned, 120 views and 276 followers, and the creator admits these views are 'not organic': they come from an app where users watch each other's videos. Rumble is reported to have no follower or watch-hour minimum for basic monetization, unlike YouTube, but the earnings shown are tiny and exchange-driven, and a guide plus app link are offered only by DM after a comment (lead-magnet funnel). Whether this complies with Rumble's rules was not confirmed.

title: Four risky websites for phones and OTPs
author: briefonlive
key_info: The reel misdescribes the sites. NumLookup is a reverse phone lookup service, not a way to call people without showing your number. SMS24 and YOPmail are public disposable number and email inboxes: real, but anyone can read the messages, and many apps block them. The fourth site is a call and SMS bombing tool, which is harassment and should not be used on anyone's phone. The caption itself adds safety disclaimers the voiceover lacks. Do not use these for banking, sensitive accounts or anything you need to recover.

title: Faceless channel on trending Netflix shows
author: scottsmithyta
key_info: The viewership figure is close to reported data (Monster: The Ed Gein Story debuted with about 12.2M views, over roughly three days rather than four). The $3,078 monthly earnings of an unnamed 'small channel' and the cost of about $75 per video are the creator's own claims with no channel or proof shown. The post ends with a 'Comment Training' lead magnet. The three prompts were on slides that were not captured.

title: Open-source Higgsfield AI alternative
author: futureproof_hacks
key_info: The repo is real: an MIT-licensed open-source image and video generation studio (Open Generative AI by Anil-matcha, about 31k stars when checked), and the reel shows a fork (Autom8AI/Open-Higgsfield-AI) rebranded as a Higgsfield alternative. The software is free, but 'unlimited videos for free' is misleading: cloud generation goes through a third-party API (Muapi in the original, kie.ai in the fork's commit messages) that needs an API key and has its own pricing, and local generation needs a capable GPU. Link was only given via bio or DM.

title: Cloudflare Code Mode MCP explained
author: decoding_tech_
key_info: Cloudflare's Code Mode is real: its MCP server exposes the whole Cloudflare API through two tools (search and execute), where the model writes code instead of calling many tool definitions, which Cloudflare says takes about 1,000 tokens against about 1.17 million for an equivalent standard MCP server. The 'companies are moving away from MCP' headline is overstated: Code Mode still runs as an MCP server, so it optimises MCP rather than replacing it. 'Other companies are following' was not checked.

title: Meta Muse will make millionaires hype
author: pranavbytes
key_info: Meta's Muse Spark model is real (launched April 2026), but the video's 'millionaires' framing is a quoted prediction (a tweet by Greg Isenberg saying Meta Muse will probably create 1000+ millionaires), not a result. The video gives no method: it ends by asking you to comment to get a free 'guide' by DM, a lead-magnet funnel. Part of a 'Day 6/100' series.

title: OpenArt Director short films for YouTube
author: magicwithsanti
key_info: Pitches turning ChatGPT scripts into AI short films with OpenArt Director as an alternative to a part-time job. Director is a real, paid OpenArt feature, but the income angle is unproven and the caption itself says there are no guaranteed results.

title: Claude Code software factory demo
author: zazencodes
key_info: A sponsored demo (by Anthropic) of a Claude Code 'software factory': a loop of spec writer, builder, review sub-agents (UX, UI, security, code quality) and an approver that merges or escalates to a human. The building blocks are real Claude Code features; the shown result is one demo and was not independently checked.

title: ComfyUI for local AI media
author: justinmendez.ai
key_info: ComfyUI is a real, free, open-source node-based engine for image, video and audio generation that runs on your own hardware, so there are no per-generation credits. The '5.6 million downloads' figure could not be confirmed, and you need a capable GPU for the heavy models.

title: Understand Anything codebase knowledge graph
author: dailydoseofds_
key_info: Understand Anything is a real open-source (MIT) plugin that builds an interactive knowledge graph of a codebase with a multi-agent pipeline, with commands such as /understand and /understand-dashboard. The repo showed about 87k GitHub stars when checked, consistent with the post's 86k+. The repo link was in the comments, which were not fetched; install steps are in the repo README.

title: 3 free AI video generators
author: himanshhh.ai
key_info: A reel naming three AI video generators as free: MiniMax, Hailuo and Tencent's Hunyuan. All three have some free access, but the limits are small, watermarked or hardware-heavy, and the tool names in the audio are partly garbled.

title: Air fryer chicken fajitas
author: coach_brettcarrington
key_info: A high-protein air fryer chicken fajita tray for four. The caption's macros (320 kcal, 51 g protein per serving) match the calculated values within about 7%, though they exclude rice, wraps or potatoes.

title: Dark uncensored ChatGPT lure
author: hitansh.exee
key_info: A reel pitching an unnamed 'darkest uncensored ChatGPT' as day 1 of a 100-day AI side-income series, demoed with a question about converting black money to white money (laundering). The tool is never named and the link is given only by DM, so it is unverified and the framing is risky.

title: Niche page growth strategy
author: indiafounder
key_info: Strategy advice for growing a niche short-video page: pick one niche, study the top channels' best videos, then build each video for average view duration and for shareability. It is opinion and method, with no numbers to verify.

title: 20 free websites for students and developers
author: anurag.builds
key_info: A comment-for-links carousel promising 20 free browser-based sites: free textbooks and papers, university courses, a Photoshop replacement, image compressors and code-screenshot tools. Only the caption was captured, so the 20 sites are unknown.

title: Thank-you message to Tanmay Bhat
author: itshotfix
key_info: A creator's personal thank-you video to comedian Tanmay Bhat, crediting a podcast recommendation (Atomic Habits) for helping him buy a house for his parents and grow his wife's account from 500 to 140K followers. These are personal claims with no checkable evidence.

title: Podcast clipping side hustle
author: jamie.creates.8
key_info: Shows how to cut short clips from a popular YouTube podcast with the Ssemble AI clipper and post them. The 'doctor's salary' claim is not supported, and reposting someone's podcast without permission is a copyright risk.

title: OpenShorts video clipper
author: umarmullaai
key_info: OpenShorts is a real MIT-licensed, self-hosted tool that turns long videos into 9:16 shorts with captions; it runs on 8 GB RAM but needs Docker and your own Gemini, ElevenLabs and fal.ai keys, which cost money per video.

title: Whop clipping side hustle
author: maxclips01
key_info: Clipping podcast moments for pay-per-view bounties on Whop is real, but typical rates are about $1 per 1,000 verified views and beginners usually earn $100-500 a month, so 'paid my rent in 5 minutes' is misleading.

title: Oracle free cloud server
author: techie.ronniee
key_info: Oracle Cloud's Always Free tier really includes an Ampere A1 instance with up to 4 OCPUs, 24 GB RAM and 200 GB block storage, but idle instances can be reclaimed, capacity is often unavailable, and one source reports a 2026 cut that was not confirmed. The reel wrongly says 8 vCPU in the voiceover.

title: Local uncensored model meme
author: progressolabs
key_info: A meme comparing a refused request to a hosted model against a 6 GB local 'uncensored' model that complied. It names no specific model; the follow-up research covers Qwen abliterated variants, their rough hardware needs and the caveats.

title: Colab A100 with Google AI Pro
author: baljeet.ai
key_info: Google AI Pro now bundles premium Colab with A100 80GB access (per a Google Gemma post), and Jio users in India get Google AI Pro free for 18 months; the GPU runs on compute units, is not guaranteed, and whether Jio's plan includes Colab is unconfirmed.

title: Meta Muse AI free tokens
author: indlive24hrs
key_info: Meta Muse is a real personal AI agent with reported referral offers of 1 billion free tokens, but the reel's claims of long-video and automatic YouTube production are unconfirmed, availability in India is unclear, and the guide is gated behind a comment funnel.

title: Prompt for more ambitious AI work
author: chase.h.ai
key_info: Summarises Felix Rieseberg's post on being more ambitious with AI (speed, altitude, depth, range) and a four-part prompt to append to any task. The prompt matches the on-screen article text; the source page itself was not independently confirmed.

title: RAG-Anything multimodal RAG
author: dailydoseofds_
key_info: RAG-Anything is a real open-source multimodal RAG framework from the HKUDS team behind LightRAG. It parses text, images, tables and equations into a knowledge graph and retrieves across them. The post's description matches the project; the GitHub link was in the comments, which were not fetched.

title: Higgsfield Katana in Claude
author: visionaryclown.tv
key_info: Higgsfield MCP + Katana skill is real and works inside Claude, but it needs a paid Higgsfield plan (not free) and is a reference-video editing skill; the one-prompt motion-graphics demo is unproven.

title: AI tools list carousel
author: power.ai
key_info: A comment-for-links carousel of AI tools credited to Linus Ekenstam on X. Only the caption was captured, so the tools are unknown.

title: Top 10 fastest-growing Claude Skills
author: earlystartupdays
key_info: A newsletter account's carousel ranking the 10 Claude Skills that gained the most GitHub stars in September 2026. Only the caption was available, so the individual skills are not named in this note.

title: Motion design prompt repo
author: ai.with.etqad
key_info: A GitHub repo of 500+ AI motion-design prompts (MIT licence, shown on screen) that the creator only shares via a share-in-DM funnel; the repo itself could not be identified, so the claims are unverified.

title: AI YouTube channel automation
author: aiwithsanskar
key_info: Real free building blocks (Edge TTS, Pexels API, Gemini free tier) but the specific repo is unverified and the autopilot-income claim is misleading; YouTube demonetizes mass-produced AI channels.

title: FreeVideo for local AI video
author: umarmullaai
key_info: FreeVideo is a real, Apache-2.0 ComfyUI engine that runs a modified MiniMax H3 (VDN-H3) video model locally on 8 GB VRAM, but 8 GB is the minimum, it will be slow, and the model weights carry a restrictive community licence.

title: Animation Claude skills carousel
author: okaashish
key_info: A carousel promoting Claude skills, apparently for animation, with the links sent by DM after commenting 'animate'. The slides were not captured, so none of the listed skills or links were read.

title: Content creation camp promo
author: kristina_monastyrska
key_info: A creator's carousel promoting her paid 2026 content-creation system, with the caption claiming 59,000 followers and a 4-million-view post. The slides were not captured, so the carousel items themselves are unchecked.

title: SEBI PaRRVA and Univest stock tips claim
author: univest.in
key_info: SEBI's PaRRVA (Past Risk and Return Verification Agency, run by CARE Ratings with NSE as data centre) is real and was meant to curb unverified past-return claims. But the reel is posted by univest.in itself and presents the adviser's own numbers (191 trades, 92% success, 2.85% average profit, 100% success in a segment) as independent 'research' and says its recommendations are free in its app. I did not verify those numbers or the firm's registration. A research-screening prompt for Claude is included below as requested.

title: Claude makes a clinic ad video
author: logam.academy
key_info: An Indian marketing agency owner shows Claude (with Hyperframes and Remotion) writing a script and producing a 2.5-minute clinic ad in about 1.5 hours. The tools are real; the claimed saving from about 2 lakh rupees is self-reported.

title: China AI video generator
author: snnubbo
key_info: chinaai.app is a real site that bundles Seedance, Kling and Wan video models, but nothing I could read says it is free, and it names no operator, so the reel's free claim is unverified.

title: Cheaper alternatives to paid AI tools
author: alexxmarketing
key_info: A caption-only list swapping 14 paid tools for cheaper or free ones. The three swaps I checked (Cline for Cursor, n8n for Zapier, Hedra for HeyGen) have real free options, but each is an alternative with trade-offs rather than a like-for-like replacement. Most of the other pairs were not checked.

title: Grok Bot AI agents
author: shrug.manny
key_info: Grok Bot is a real paid SpaceXAI cloud-agent product in beta, and this reel is a sponsored promo: the agent set is free but running it is not, and the Tinder, LinkedIn and airline-refund automations are shown only as descriptions, not results.

title: Free Gemini Omni video generation
author: futurewalt.ai
key_info: Google did open Gemini Omni video generation to anyone with a Google account through Google Vids (vids.new), but one test reported only 720p output, so the free 1080p claim is unconfirmed. Only the caption was captured, not the post images.

title: AI influencer income pitch
author: tech_new_trends
key_info: A Telegram funnel pitching AI influencers, backed by a Google AI Overview screenshot saying Indian AI influencers earn 1 to 6 lakh rupees a month. Individual cases exist (one reported at about 1.2 lakh), but the range is an AI-generated summary and the real workflow is behind a link.

title: You Can See Everything trailer
author: a24
key_info: Official A24 trailer for the documentary You Can See Everything by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, featuring Elizabeth Holmes. In theaters October 16, 2026. No claims to check.

title: AI OnlyFans income claims called a red flag
author: jiannacapri
key_info: A creator checks viral 'AI girl' earnings posts: two accounts claim the same $49,134 using identical screenshots, Fanvue is real and allows AI personas, but the earnings figures trace back to referral-link promoters. Her verdict is a red flag.

title: Locally Uncensored local AI studio
author: gittrend.io
key_info: Locally Uncensored (PurpleDoubleD/locally-uncensored) is a real free, open-source (AGPL-3.0) desktop app that bundles local chat, image and video generation and a coding agent, for Windows and Linux (macOS beta). The repo lookup matches the reel: about 2.5k stars, actively updated, no cloud required. Results depend on your hardware and the models you pick, and the 'uncensored' models are your responsibility. The repo link is only sent by DM.

title: Krea MCP faceless YouTube side hustle
author: kenthustles
key_info: The Krea connector setup in Claude is real, but the $10k/month claim is unsupported and the post is a paid Krea partner promotion. The advice is to copy a big channel's niche and let an AI make videos.

title: 5 free AI video generators teaser
author: aitoxictales
key_info: A teaser for a longer YouTube video listing five free AI video generators; this reel never names the five tools. It only promises that one of them gives access to Seedance, Veo 3.1 and Kling models.

title: Clipping and copyright: is it safe
author: tillmann_clips
key_info: Half right: clipping for a paid campaign (Whop or Ssemble Clip Rewards) is the safe route because the owner authorises and pays for clips. But 'copyright has never been an issue' and 'just tag the creator' are not safe advice: YouTube's reused-content rules reward meaningful transformation, and credit does not by itself make reused material monetizable or licensed. The creator also promotes the tool with a discount code (TJ10) that earns them commission.

title: Emergent: sell AI-built apps to SMBs
author: casarthakahuja
key_info: Funding facts check out: Emergent, run by twin brothers Mukund and Madhav Jha, raised a $130M Series C at a $1.5B valuation. The pitch that you can learn the tool and sell custom software to small businesses is a plausible business idea but unproven: no income evidence is given, the Rs 10,000 to 80,000 website and store prices are the creator's own figures, and the post is marked #collab, so it is a paid promotion.

title: Free alternatives to paid AI tools
author: max_v.v
key_info: Two presenters pair paid AI tools with free ones (video: ArtFlow, voice cloning: FishAudio vs ElevenLabs, brainstorming: Gemini). All three free tiers exist but are limited, and the full list of 46 is behind a comment-for-DM gate.

title: Arnold on the best tricep exercise
author: PumpCrib
key_info: Clip repost of Arnold Schwarzenegger explaining his pick for the best tricep exercise. Video and audio could not be fetched, so the exercise named is not recorded.
